summary: Joey Hung works in computational and Buddhist studies. Educated at PLK Fong Wong Kam Chuen Primary School, Po Leung Kuk Centenary Li Shiu Chung Memorial College, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, he held posts at DILA (~2014) and CIBS (attested 2026).
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency University, working in Indology and history/archaeology. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College (~1908–1917), Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog works in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington under scholars including Christopher P. Atwood and Jan Nattier. He held posts at UCSB, IMASS, and Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden (under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber, he held posts at Maastricht, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Leiden University (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist who held academic appointments at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945) was a scholar in history/archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University, where he was taught by Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, and later held professorships at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a linguist educated at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He held posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano, Kadettenkorps München, Bavarian State Library, and the University of Munich, where he became professor in 1828.

Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a scholar of linguistics. Over his career, he held posts at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1814–1819), Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) worked in linguistics. He was educated at the Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and held posts at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787–1806).
Johann Elias Schlegel (1719–1749) was a German scholar who studied at Schulpforta (~1733–1739) and the University of Leipzig (~1739–1742).

Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander (1829–1864) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1853–1854) and Tübingen (1857–1860).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840) worked in history and archaeology. After studies at Ernestinum Gotha, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen, he held an academic post at the University of Göttingen from ~1775 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart (1776–1841) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797) and held a long-term academic post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1841).

Johann Gildemeister (1812–1890) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Georg Freytag, Christian Lassen, and A. W. von Schlegel, later holding professorships at the University of Marburg (~1844–1859) and University of Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn (1752–1827) was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, he held professorships at the University of Jena (1775) and the University of Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten (1792–1860) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Greifswald and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850).

Johann Gottfried von Herder (1744–1803) studied philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies at the University of Königsberg under Immanuel Kant. His career included posts at Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, the Court of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, and Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar.

Johann Gustav Stickel (1805–1896) worked in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena under Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, serving as professor at Jena from 1830 to 1836.
Johann II Bernoulli (1710–1790) studied at the University of Basel (~1724–1729) and later held an academic post there from ~1736 to 1790.
